author: Juzam
subject: Re: Please make Aimed shot worth using
content_md:
Getting rid of Aimed shot in PVE rotation is the best thing who could have happened.

AS force you to use super slow weapons to get the best dps even if faster weapons with better dps are available.

In Twow, it would prevent the use of haste items or fast weapons to get more Improved aspects of the Hawk procs.

Aimed shot is now an opener just like Ambush which is fine.

The other direction Twow could have taken to revamp hunter would have been, instead of adding trueshot, to make stings and traps scale on AP (or RAP) and arcane shot based on weapon damage normalised at 2.8 (which also would have helped hunter in pvp because hunter is the worst ranged class regarding to the ability of doing damage while moving, others have much better instants or dots to apply while moving).

But they choosed Trueshot, and it work great for PVE.

author: Atreidon
subject: Re: Please make Aimed shot worth using
content_md:
I think the hunters rotation at the moment leaves a lot to be desired. Adding trueshot was a good move, but its so good it pushed aimed shot out of the rotation. Aimed shot is an ability that demands to be used skillfully (not cast it when you are about to get hit by aoe, watch the swingtimer etc) and is a  huge dopamine spike. It being not worth using is really sad.

It also doesn't function as an opener, or rather hunter has no use for openers in such a reagard. Since your target in PvP will get you as their target if you start casting on them from an unexpected angle. While in PvE the threatspike is undesirable to the point of just sending in the pet and starting to shoot is preferable 99% of the time.

Ranged attackspeed haste also improves the cast time of Aimed shot, The haste argument is mute.

But Trueshot does make fast weapons a bit more enticing to play with (even tho i still don't think they outperform slow ones). Which is overall a welcome change.
Its a tough one to fix. Nerfing Trueshot to give aimed room is just nerfing hunter so one ability gets to shine again. Which i don't think is necessarily a good choice either.

content_md:
My opinion, at this point in the game, the aiming shot for PvP is rarely used, or maybe even stopped using it altogether. The reason for this is that many classes have instant spells that do more damage. Compare the damage at warlock, mage pro shaman with earthshock in 1500 krit and it's all instant, you will now say they have a small radius I will argue you hunters have always had an advantage is the range of fire, when they added talents for distance hunter lost the advantage. About the synchronisation on the server in general I do not say, the player receives a stun and with it still moves 1 sec. For this reason alone I am ‘FOR’ to remove the dead zone, or rework the aiming shot.
You compare who is playing now on BG, Shamans, paladins and warriors the rest are echoes.  It's not whining, it's facts. If we want balance in the game we need to listen and try.

author: FrankFankledank
subject: Re: arrows and bullets
content_md:
Let me recontextualize this for you:

The biggest quiver in the game offers less than half as much space as the largest regular bag. You are not only using 16 slots for ammo, but also the loss of regular bag slots from the incredibly prevalent 18-22 slotters now littered in raiding content, if not the massive 20 slot loss from not using a turtle shop bag.

Vanilla philosophy generally has specialized bags either matching the highest available regular bag size but with much easier acquirement, or a larger size. A Warlock's soul bag can go as high as 28 slots in core Vanilla, where 18 slots were the absolute pinnacle. Warlocks (who had multiple buffs to their Soul Shard stacking) can also restock their "ammo" in any similarly-levelled zone, whereas a Hunter needs to go to one of two very specific boss fights to get their top-tier ammo, which their best quiver can only hold about 3 runs' worth at a time. The cash shop ammo vendor doesn't change this, it doesn't even offer the second (AV quartermaster ammo) or third (Engineer-crafted Thorium ammo) best types, only basic white vendor stuff.

author: Stian
subject: Hunter Rework Concept
content_md:
Hi all,
Hunter has been my first choice of class for about 20 years now. However, playing one on twow I find a less appealing idea. Sure they have a melee spec, but meleeing as a hunter always feels a bit like dating someone that is too young for you - sure they are cute and it can be nice, but there is always that feeling of weirdness to it. Having played tons of vanilla and then SoD, it is hard going back to a vanillaish hunter style again, so now I play as a hunter priest - namely the nelf kind, and I'm loving it!

A lot of people seem less then pleased with the BM rework (saucy sausage) and the generic nature of pets. So.. I made the following talent trees for the hunter specs (please keep in mind that this is poorly balanced and it is more conceptual at this stage):

[https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c ... ?points=--](https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/calculator/l3KCnHvWvf?points=--)

My aim is to have three quite distinct types of hunter being available to the player.

The BM spec is heavily focused on your pet and becoming one with the beast, most specs would want to spec into the aspect line in the BM tree.

Marksmanship is your ranger/archer and even spell ranger type.

Survival is the melee tree for your brawny Rexxar type, troll/orc axe thrower and/or your trappy forethought sneaky maniac. They offer added utility, can take a hit and hit hard themselves while having some added CC.

These three trees could support a wide variety of hunter playstyles. You can go full BM and get the melee talents in Surs, go BM/MM hybrid (focusing on either), Surv/BM, Full MM (picking up aspect talents from BM and tier 1 talents from Surv - including Lone Wolf), have an AoE farming off-spec by taking trap talents in Surv and filling out MM (picking Barrage for increased AoE dmg), Picking the survivability and CC talents in Surv and buffing your pet and defensive aspects in BM for a dungeon tank hunter and so on..

I wanted to frontload most talents so that you can start playing your spec as early as possible. As the trees are now, they would surely make hunters OP, so yes please thank you (just kidding, but not really).

 **Some things to clear up,**
 **-** A lot of changes to pets that I will detail below this section.

 **-** No more dead zone. The minimum range for ranged attack is equal to the max melee range. Switching between the two modes of attack does not happen automatically.

 **-** Change Arcane Shot into Quick Shot as the whole spell dmg shot thing is enabled via the MM tree, and Arcane Shot doesn't make sense for BM or Surv. You can turn your Quick Shot into an Arcane Shot with MM talents anyway. Could consider having it not share a CD with Aimed Shot, but the idea of making a choice between taking your time to line up an aimed shot vs taking a quick pop is quite nice.

 **-** Aimed shot chance is to make ranged wpn speed less relevant (maybe most shots should also be reworked to rely more on ranged attack power instead of wpn dmg) and to make it more interactive (might be affected by the point below). Flurry Fire would feel amazing I think, and makes sense for both (machine) guns and bows (repeating xbow anyone?).

 **-** Some of my ideas might not be possible to implement at all due to how the game works.

 **-** There would be class quests to unlock any type of aspect, akin to shaman's class quests for totems. One thing that feels most meaningful in wow are class quests. There would also be an aspect for every kind of beast.

 **-** Hunters would have class professions, like rogues do: Fletching, Poisons and Trapping.
Fletching could also be Munitions and Hunters here craft their own ammo, I prefer keeping gun ammo for the engi professions as it does fit there and belongs alongside mining. Arrows would be crafted using drops like feathers, bones, etc. maybe add a rope crafting thing in the survivalist profession for arrow construction. Poisons would be unlocking stings and crafting them.

Wanna use Scorpid Sting? Go and farm some poison from scorpions. Best I feel if this profession is low resource intensity, 1 poison drop makes a gazillion poison shots. Trapping would be trap crafting, from wood, steel, oil, rope and the rune/magic traps some magic juju items.

 **-** Hunters would get their pets much earlier. The 1-10 brackets for hunters is a very strange sort of pre-life. The transition from kite firing auto shot to having your pet become the main character and you a turret is also a strange one, though. Maybe growl is just less of a thing, so now you have to kite and use your CC toolkit with the new Snare Trap (smells like short cute class quest!) being available at lvl 1?

At level one, a series of quests will be available to you from your class trainer. You pick one (like in pokemon) and this is will lead you to your first pet and pet type and aspect. https://talent-builder.haaxor1689.dev/c ... ?points=--


My aim is to have three quite distinct types of hunter being available to the player.

The BM spec is heavily focused on your pet and becoming one with the beast, most specs would want to spec into the aspect line in the BM tree.

Marksmanship is your ranger/archer and even spell ranger type.

Survival is the melee tree for your brawny Rexxar type, troll/orc axe thrower and/or your trappy forethought sneaky maniac. They offer added utility, can take a hit and hit hard themselves while having some added CC.

author: Lane13
subject: Feedback: Kill Command range and other issues
content_md:
Kill Command has a range of 45 yards. While it may look like it's enough, it's not. On bosses with big arenas where you and your pet will be in very different spots, you won't reach your pet with it. There's a reason why both Intimidation and Bestial Wrath have a range of 100 yards so Kill Command should also be in this position.

Of course, fix the BM bugs that have been reported since day one related to Kill Command and Baited Shot.

Kill Command should also not require LoS and remove silences from pets, as a silence is essentially a CC ability for families such as wind serpents and scorpids, who rely on their spells for damage.

Finally, another request I have is to remove the LoS requirement for the Breastplate of Beast Mastery and the Unseen Path bonuses, as they can clog the screen with LoS errors and make no sense in the first place. The bonuses should always be active as long as you're wearing the gear and your pet is alive, like it happens with the Beastmaster's Boots. Additionally, clarify if all the pet % bonuses from different items should stack or not, since right now there are bug reports explaining how this is not the case and how some of them cancel each other out constantly.

author: Soulforged23
subject: MM not in a good spot...
content_md:
I ve been playing my MM hunter for a while now, and despite the devs previously saying the spec is in a good spot, the reality is a completely different story. I also play a couple other classes, and the difference is night and day. While on my other chars I feel powerful, on my hunter, I have to sweat even with players wish same gear and even below to use every single trick in the book just to survive a 1v1, and even then it feels like an uphill battle.

The core of the problem is that our abilities simply havent kept up with the power creep of other classes. Take aimed Shot, for example. In any other class, a long cast time like pyroblast rewards you with massive damage. For us? aimed Shot is basically a trap. You can use it as an opener, but once the fight starts, you re better off just using autoshots and Steady Shot because the dps is better and it doesn’t have a ridiculous wind up for a non guaranteed crit. Its insane that we have a signature big hit that hits like a wet noodle. Whether it needs to be a guaranteed crit or a proc based instant cast something has to change because right now it’s a dead button on the bar.

Our scaling is also nonexistent. Arcane Shot and volley are jokes because they don't scale with attack power. Seeing Arcane Shot hit for 183 damage at high levels is embarrassing. Serpent sting is even worse...imagine spending 5 talent points just to have a dot that deals negligible damage. Meanwhile, trueshot Aura our ultimate 31 is just a weak aura compared to the massive damage abilities other classes get, like the warlocks dark harvest. We are reduced to a steady shot bot rotation that feels static and unrewarding.

The situation in PvP is even more dire. The 3 sec cooldown on wing clip combined with the removal of counterattack has completely crippled our ability to manage the deadzone. If a rogue or a warrior gets on you, you re basically done. Between the new custom foods like sweet n crunchy fruit bread that let Rogues ignore freezes, and Sprint bypassing traps, we have almost no way to escape anymore. It feels like the devs nerfed our CC because of the survival rework but completely forgot that MM hunters still need those tools to function at a baseline level.

The numbers dont lie either. Seeing hunters at the bottom of the charts in turtle logs, is a slap in the face for a pure DPS class. Every other class has 2k damage skills now while we are stuck with vanilla values and broken animations. Our shooting mechanics make us too static, mutlishot requiring us to stand still for an instant is clunky, traps share DR with Scatter, we los our autoshot rotation in corners while channeling spells go through walls.

We need more than just minuscule talent tweaks. Ranged hunter needs a serious look at its scaling, its utility, and its ulti abilities. We shouldnt have to lose all our utility and identity just to do baseline damage. Hopefully, someone on the dev team is actually looking at hunter feedback, because right now it feels like the class is being left in the dust while everyone else gets to play a modern version of the game.

author: Somersby
subject: Re: MM not in a good spot...
content_md:
Currently, Hunters in PvP (I'm considering BM and MM; I haven't played the Survival specialization, as I believe Hunter = ranged combat) are slightly stronger than Dummys in capital cities.

Hunters' entire gameplay revolved around controlling targets at a distance, aided by the "Hawk Eye" talent. Among other things, they had the "Counterattack" ability, which was removed in favor of the Survival specialization's AoE abilities. They increased the cooldown on "Wing Clip" but increased its damage ("Survival" is all about you). Simply put, Hunters were stripped of all their survival abilities...for the sake of "Survival." It was pretty funny.

Hunter damage is a whole other pain in the ass. No one will argue that it's negligible compared to other classes. But mindlessly increasing it by n% risks skewing the PvE aspect of the game. I can't boast of any significant raiding experience. I've currently completed all available raids on the Ambershire server in the BM specialization in Pugo Raids. So, I wouldn't dare say from personal experience that Hunters are the last in the DPS class in PVE. Experienced players who have completed Naxxramas on Nordanaar feel free to correct me.

Nevertheless, changes are urgently needed. As the saying goes, "When criticizing, suggest":

 **Marksmanship Specialization**

- Combining the two talents "Improved Stings" and "Improved Scorpid Sting" into a single talent seems logical;

- Replace the "Improved Scorpid Sting" talent with a new talent: "Enchanted Arrows" - allows the Hunter to enchant arrows with one of three possible effects:
Frost Arrows: Auto-attacks have a chance to fire a Frost Arrow (a magical attack that ignores armor), slowing the target by 30-40%;

Poison Arrow: Auto-attacks have a chance to extend the duration of an existing "Serpent Sting" by 3 or 6 seconds;

Fire Arrow: Auto-attacks have a chance to ignite the target and nearby enemies, dealing 50-150 Fire damage (slightly increased AoE);

- Add to the "Improved Steady Shot" talent: Critical strikes grant the Hunter a stacking buff that reduces the cast time of "Aimed Shot" by 20%. Stacks up to 5 times.

- Adjust "Endless Quiver": increase the proc chance to 5/10%, and the shot will now deal MAGIC damage.
 **Beast Mastery Specialization**

- Add "Improved Primal Aspects" talent: while Aspect of the Hawk is active, your attacks ignore 100/200/300 armor;

- Add "Ferocity" talent: pet critical strikes restore 2/4/6/8/10% of the damage dealt;

- "Beastly Discipline" talent: the cooldown reduction effect should apply to both "KIll Command" and "Intimidate."

- "Baited Shot" talent: change weapon-based scaling to ranged attack power-based scaling.
 **General Changes:**

- Reintroduce the "Counterattack" ability for all specializations, with the same effect but with fixed damage.

- New ability "Master's Call": Your pet rushes to the aid of a target (you or an ally) and removes all slows. Cooldown: 1 minute.  Warriors now have the "Improved Berserker Rage" talent in the "Fury" talent tree, and Ferals now have a full-fledged reshift. Why can't Hunters get a version of "Master's Call" from WOTLK?

- Arcane shot: Make damage scale with ranged attack power
These changes won't significantly impact PVE, although they will be useful there as well. However, in PVP, I think Hunters will be stronger.

I've tried to summarize my thoughts very briefly, although I have much more to say about many aspects of Hunter play. In any case, I really want to see the Turtle team's opinion on hunters, since "We believe Marksmanship is in a good spot. We are considering taking another look at the design of Trueshot Aura and possibly at Volley in a future update, but for now we don't believe the specialization needs any change." seems like a joke.

P.S. English is not my native language. I apologize if Google Translate gave me some nonsense.

content_html:
I ve been playing my MM hunter for a while now, and despite the devs previously saying the spec is in a good spot, the reality is a completely different story. I also play a couple other classes, and the difference is night and day. While on my other chars I feel powerful, on my hunter, I have to sweat even with players wish same gear and even below to use every single trick in the book just to survive a 1v1, and even then it feels like an uphill battle.

The core of the problem is that our abilities simply havent kept up with the power creep of other classes. Take aimed Shot, for example. In any other class, a long cast time like pyroblast rewards you with massive damage. For us? aimed Shot is basically a trap. You can use it as an opener, but once the fight starts, you re better off just using autoshots and Steady Shot because the dps is better and it doesn’t have a ridiculous wind up for a non guaranteed crit. Its insane that we have a signature big hit that hits like a wet noodle. Whether it needs to be a guaranteed crit or a proc based instant cast something has to change because right now it’s a dead button on the bar.

Our scaling is also nonexistent. Arcane Shot and volley are jokes because they don't scale with attack power. Seeing Arcane Shot hit for 183 damage at high levels is embarrassing. Serpent sting is even worse...imagine spending 5 talent points just to have a dot that deals negligible damage. Meanwhile, trueshot Aura our ultimate 31 is just a weak aura compared to the massive damage abilities other classes get, like the warlocks dark harvest. We are reduced to a steady shot bot rotation that feels static and unrewarding.

The situation in PvP is even more dire. The 3 sec cooldown on wing clip combined with the removal of counterattack has completely crippled our ability to manage the deadzone. If a rogue or a warrior gets on you, you re basically done. Between the new custom foods like sweet n crunchy fruit bread that let Rogues ignore freezes, and Sprint bypassing traps, we have almost no way to escape anymore. It feels like the devs nerfed our CC because of the survival rework but completely forgot that MM hunters still need those tools to function at a baseline level.

The numbers dont lie either. Seeing hunters at the bottom of the charts in turtle logs, is a slap in the face for a pure DPS class. Every other class has 2k damage skills now while we are stuck with vanilla values and broken animations. Our shooting mechanics make us too static, mutlishot requiring us to stand still for an instant is clunky, traps share DR with Scatter, we los our autoshot rotation in corners while channeling spells go through walls.

We need more than just minuscule talent tweaks. Ranged hunter needs a serious look at its scaling, its utility, and its ulti abilities. We shouldnt have to lose all our utility and identity just to do baseline damage. Hopefully, someone on the dev team is actually looking at hunter feedback, because right now it feels like the class is being left in the dust while everyone else gets to play a modern version of the game.
Word for word what I wrote in previous posts and this can't be denied. Every hunter I talk to said the same thing. I REALLY hope they listen because this are not empty words and whining. This comes from real place and experience. While hunter is my main, I play other classes, and that experience showed me that hunters are WAAAAY behind other classes. Even other classes that don't play hunters have agreed.

author: Hctwowfan
subject: Re: Pet training points gain rate incredibly slow?
content_md:
The formula for training points (tp) is:

Pet level x (Pet loyalty - 1) = current tp

Max tp is 300:
 60 x (6 - 1) = 300

If your pet gains a level, it gains tp equal to pet loyalty -1.
If your pet gains loyalty, it gains tp equal to its level.

At 30 gaining a level at 6 loyalty:
 30 x 5 = 150 --> 31 x 5 = 155

At 30 gaining loyalty from 4 to 5 (or 5 to 6, doesn't matter, absolute increase is the same):
 30 x 3 = 90 --> 30 x 4 = 120

Everything works as it did in vanilla.

Edit: Your pet will not be able to learn every available ability and passive ever. Max stamina and max armor already take up most of your max tp. Abilities are rather cheap in that regard. Resistances have to be spread across multiple pets for that matter. Have a pet with fire resistance maxed, one with frost resistance, one with nature, one with arcane basically.

author: Metasploit
subject: [Add-on] Introducing MetaHunt
content_md:
**MetaHunt**
 *Twow Hunter's Toolkit*

![Image](https://i.ibb.co/35r5MRkC/image.png)

Hey fellow hunters

Here's a project I have been working on for some weeks and I am happy with the results so its time to release it.

MetaHunt is an addon 100% Hunter and 100% Turtle WoW. English-only atm.

It ships with large datastore of twow data, revives some old good but broken addons (zHunterMod and Feed-O-Matic), and introduce never seen ammo management and pet-centric features.

---
Twow Data

Metahunt ships with a large up-to-date datastore containing all Turtle WOW data a hunter needs :

- All beasts, their location, and the abilities they can learn you
- All Pet families, their abilities and their diet
- All pet abilities ranks
- All ranged weapons, Arrows, Bullets, Quivers and Pouches.
- All Stable, Hunter and Pet Masters
- All Ammo vendors

---
Smart Ammo

- Auto swap your main ammo to junk ammo for shots that doesn't scale on damage, and re-equip you main ammo right away. Don't waste your Doomshots on nothing anymore, save money ! Just make sure you have some rough arrows in your quiver.
- Auto equip another ammo instantly during combat whenever you get out of your current ammo.
- Auto equip the right ammo when you swap from a bow/xbow to a gun and the other way around.

---
Tooltips

Get enhanced mouseover tooltips on :

- Beasts : Shows which abilities a beast can teach. They appear green if you already know them, and red if not.
- Vendors : Shows if a vendor sells Arrows and/or Bullets.
- Your pet : Shows your pet's XP, loyalty, happiness and how much you fed it this session.

---
zBouttons

Old zHunterMod addon on steroids. Fully compatible with Twow, and enhanced with new functionalities

- zAmmo : Track all your ammo Live and swap them in a click or bind
- zPet : collapsible pet Bar regrouping all pet spells and providing an intelligent parent button that always shows you the right spell to use depending on the situation
- zTrack: All your trackings in one collapsible bar
- zAspect: All your Aspects in one collapsible bar, the parent toggle from your primary choice to your 2nd
- zRanged : All the ranged weapons currently in your bags to swap them fast
- But also zMounts, zToys and zCompanions.
[![Image](https://i.ibb.co/dJW0zwMq/zbars.png)](https://imgbb.com/)

---
Feed-O-Matic

Now compatible with Turtle, feed your pet with one key bind, it will always pickup the best food for your pet.
 *Note that I haven't reviewed at all all cooking/quest/bufffood stuff because I am lacking the necessary data. The Turtle  DB is just impossible to fetch on food in the actual state.*

---
Chronometer

The good old Chronometer addon, purged of non-necessary things, dealing with all hunters spells and HL trinkets and reconfigured for a pure hunter use.

---
Autobuy

Define your own simple rules to auto buy ammo and/or pet food when you open a vendor that sells anything of it

---
ICU (I see you)

Old addon used to display Targets' enhanced information when you click on your minimap tracking things. MetaHunt offers many more customization options for it.

---
Auto-Quest

Just spam SHIFT-click on the NPC to validate quests Scorpok and Thorium arrows. Additionally you can have an enhanced tooltip that display your actual Scorpok-related items when you mouseover the mobs involved.

---
The Great Book of Huntards

The book of Hunters is the main GUI of MetaHunt, it allows to display the data constantly collected about you and your pet, and browse the addon's data to find anything a Hunter needs.
- Browse the Metahunt datastores of NPCs (Beast, vendors, masters) and open the map to locate them like in pfQuest
- Track all info about the pet abilities that you know and don't know yet
- Track all info about your stabled pets
- Keep an history of all your pets after you abandon them or if they run away.
- Get all info about ranged weapons, ammo ad ammo bags currently in the game.
[![Image](https://i.ibb.co/Sq52mCs/book1.png)](https://ibb.co/VXJdC4j)

[![Image](https://i.ibb.co/gFJdvZ7Z/book2.png)](https://ibb.co/qFpC0YnY)

[![Image](https://i.ibb.co/xSMk51T2/book3.png)](https://ibb.co/mCHjz9WR)

[![Image](https://i.ibb.co/wF0m93mn/book4.png)](https://ibb.co/C31GkNGj)

---
Small glimpse at the option panel....
[![Image](https://i.ibb.co/wZY7TkrM/options.png)](https://ibb.co/7xbQHfN2)

You can download it on GitHub, and as usual, remove the "-master" from the folder name.
<https://github.com/DuvelCorp/MetaHunt>

Have a nice hunting session.

subject: Re: [Add-on] Introducing MetaHunt
content_md:
**Credits**

This addon is, in others, a compilation of old vanilla addons that I loved and played with during years. But most of them had become very buggy with TwoW as new contain was added to the server.

I fixed, reworked, enhanced, and melted them within a modern modular framework that I created.

I want to make it crystal clear about what work is mine, and what is not and respectfully credit the original authors for the great stuff I've taken from them

 **About the code**

- zBars, Antidaze and Autostrip were core functionalities of Vanilla [zHunterMod](https://www.wowinterface.com/downloads/info6598-ZHunterMod.html) addon. And I kept the "z" naming of bars/buttons to always remember it. On top of this I have created myself zAmmo, zRanged, zCompanions, zMount, zToys.
Also the SmartAmmo swap-junk feature idea is coming from Zhuntermod: there was a file in it with that functionality, but was like a work-in-progress, totally unfunctional and even "dangerous" in its current state, and was not active in the addon. Since it was a fucking great idea, I recoded it mostly from scratch and made it work reliably and safely.
- [Feed-o-Matic](https://www.wowinterface.com/downloads/info4160-FizzwidgetFeed-O-Matic.html) was entirely the work of Fizzwidget. I made it work for Twow, by melting it as a module calling Metahunt core to get pet's state and up-to-date data for new pet families and their diet.
- Tooltips module is based on [Hunter Helper](https://legacy-wow.com/vanilla-addons/fizzwidget-hunter-helper/), another vanilla addon of Fizzwidget. I kept the general idea, but there's not much original code left from it in Metahunt as I refactored everything so it plugs on MetaHunt controlled event handlers, can work with Turtle wow data, and is now usable on other things than Beasts.
- **Chronometer** was an old and very popular vanilla addon working with ACE2 libraries. It has known uncountable iterations by various people over the years, and I can't credit them all of them here. The current version used by Metahunt is based on [this Twow conversion made by "wigan91"](https://github.com/wigan91/Chronometer-TWoW). I have reworked it to have it Hunter-focused-only: removed the non-hunter/race stuff, added hunter trinkets, improved the definition for spells/effects config that were not correct, added missing hunter spells (not many), and implemented my own bar color scheme fitting better the hunter spells.
- The Map/Marker system is the one of pfQuest from Master Shagu. Unfortunately he is no more reachable for some months and I could not have some talk with him about this. I mostly let it untouched, I just made slight modifications so it can integrate better within Metahunt, and doesn't conflict with pfQuest.
- The system allowing to fetch itemlinks in game (In the Weapon tab of the Hunter Book notably) is the one of [Atlas Twow](https://github.com/Otari98/Atlas).
 **About data sources**

Metahunt ships with its own Turtle-WoW datastores, limited to hunter stuff only, and most of this data is up-to-date (Feb 2026).

Sources used to build the data include:

- pfQuest for Beasts and Ammo vendors NPCs and their spawn points (and beasts respawn times if any). Thank you again Shagu.
- [This invaluable and very accurate spreadsheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1NbwgI9kuGvAXlfD-tpoXZ2VMwtsUBwPMhI1yrQKgeaU/edit?gid=0#gid=0) for beasts having pet abilities. A big thanks to **Destrose** that crafted this! The Great Book of Huntards is great and accurate also because of YOU.
- Atlas twow for ranged weapon sources
 **With that being said, go back hunting fellas!**

Metasploit <Atlantis>, of Nordaanar.

author: Skurridizo
subject: PETS - Problems and why Beast Mastery is not optimal
content_md:
> ****If you don’t know me, read this introduction. If you already know me, skip to point 1.****

At the very end I will propose some realistic solutions related to the problems explained below.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

 ****Hello, I’m Skurridizo.****

I’m one of the players who has explored hunter pets in Turtle WoW the most — if not the one who has done it the most.

I’m a huge fan of the class and currently have **FOUR level 60 hunters** across different Turtle WoW servers.

I also run **two YouTube channels** dedicated to sharing hunter knowledge specifically for Turtle WoW.

Right now I’m playing **Survival** more than any other spec in **Karazhan 40** and **Naxxramas**, but until recently I always played:

 ****Beast Mastery****

This specialization rewards player skill through small details and makes it the most complex of the three specs — and in my opinion the most fun.

Unfortunately this talent tree is overshadowed by Survival, and many Karazhan 40 mechanics punish it heavily, almost as if the dungeon was designed specifically to discourage playing this spec.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

> ****POINT 1 — Stable Slots****

Many people think having **4 + 1 stable slots** is more than enough.

 **The answer is obviously NO.**

Just like tanks swap gear pieces for different situations, there is no single pet that is the best in every scenario.

> Pet swapping is mandatory if you want to get real value from Beast Mastery.

Here are some examples of pets I tamed, leveled to 60, and eventually abandoned.

All of them are **BiS within their family** because they have the fastest attack speed.

> • Broken Tooth (2 times) – Level 37 rare with ~7h respawn
>  • Spirit Fox (1 time) – Level 53 rare with +48h respawn
>  • Ravage (1 time) – Level 51 rare with 15h respawn
>  • Ravasaur Matriarch (2 times) – Level 53 rare with 15h respawn
>  • Gretheer (2 times) – Level 57 rare with 50h respawn
>  • Lavender Mana Wyrm – Level 7 Wind Serpent from the High Elf starting zone
>  BiS in PvP because its tiny size makes it almost invisible

This is only a small portion of the countless pets I had to find in their BiS version, spend hours leveling to 60, and later discover they were not actually worth it.

 **Ideally required pets:**

> • Bear — Support playstyle
>  • Wolf — AoE farming + offensive support
>  • Slow Raptor — BiS DPS for Marksmanship
>  • Fast Raptor — BiS DPS for Survival
>  • Fast Scorpion — BiS Beast Mastery DPS in most situations
>  • Slow Scorpion — BiS BM/MM DPS in many situations
>  • Wind Serpent — Best option when Scorpion doesn't work / BiS PvP BM
>  • Spider — BiS PvP outside Beast Mastery
>  • Cat — Required for some raid skips
>  • Cobra / Bat / Tallstrider — Solo content and niche situations

Everything else becomes forgotten or sub-optimal.

 **My current stable:**

> Bear
>  Fast Raptor
>  Wolf
>  Fast Scorpion
>  Slow Raptor

 ****I am still missing several important ones.****

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

> ****POINT 2 — Training Difficulty****

In later expansions hunters could tame a low level pet and it would automatically scale to:

 **Player Level -5**

Meaning you only needed to level the last five levels.

Now try leveling the BiS bear:

 **Ursol'Lok**

> Level 32 rare
>  15 hour respawn timer

What happens?

> • You spend an entire day camping the spawn
>  • Then at least 10 hours leveling it to 60
>  • And it consumes a massive amount of food (gold)

I did this a few months ago.

Almost nobody else will do it because the effort does not justify the result compared to a regular Winterspring level 60 bear.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

> ****POINT 3 — Talents That Don’t Fit****

There are some items that increase pet damage such as:

<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60784>
<https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=22061>

These were useful when you were a **fresh level 60** raiding:

> Molten Core
>  Onyxia
>  Blackwing Lair

But today the situation is simple:

> **+9 Agility already gives more value than increasing your pet damage.**

 **Why does this happen?**

In WoW Classic pets had almost no real scaling.

Turtle WoW introduced new talents that try to solve this.

The most important one is:

 ****SPIRIT BOND****

> • 25% of your Ranged Attack Power → Pet Attack Power
>  • 15% of your Ranged Attack Power → Pet Spell Power
>  • Small health regeneration in combat

Beast Mastery revolves entirely around maximizing this talent.

Because of this, the pets that deal the most damage today are the ones that scale with **Spell Power**:

> Cobra
>  Scorpion
>  Wind Serpent
>  Gorilla

The Gorilla can mostly be ignored because:

> • Poor scaling
>  • 40 second cooldown ability

 **Current pet damage talents:**

> Improved Eyes of the Beast → +30% damage (but you stop attacking)
>  Unleashed Fury → +20% damage
>  Coordinated Assault → scales from hunter melee AP instead of pet
>  Ferocity → +15% crit
>  Frenzy → +30% attack speed
>  Spirit Bond
>  Baited Shot → +15% damage
>  Kill Command → GCD + huge mana cost

 **Only Spirit Bond actually scales with gear.**

And that scaling is simply not enough for late-game content.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

> ****POINT 4 — Late Game Gear Problems****

Beast Mastery benefits most from **Ranged Attack Power**.

However many items in:

> Naxxramas
>  Karazhan 40

trade attack power for **critical strike**.

This improves the hunter’s personal DPS but does almost nothing for the pet.

Additionally:

> Tier 0.5
>  Tier 1
>  Tier 2

had useful defensive bonuses for pets.

These bonuses disappear completely in:

> Tier 3
>  Tier 3.5

There is only one bonus:

> +50 Attack Power for hunter and pet

But the current meta favors **Spell Power scaling pets**.

 **A survivability bonus for pets would be far more valuable.**

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

> ****POINT 5 — Pet Survivability****

In raids almost no healers keep pet frames visible.

So hunters are expected to heal their own pets.

The problem is the spell:

 ****Mend Pet****

> 5 second channel
>  480 mana
>  1225 total healing
>  20 yard range

 **This spell is extremely inefficient.**

Even with the improved talent version it remains terrible.

A healer can outperform it with one instant GCD.

Because of this the most valuable skill becomes:

 **perfect pet positioning.**

But many mechanics still kill pets regardless:

> Void zones
>  Thaddius Tesla charges
>  Kruul cleave
>  Chess knight cleaves
>  Heigan explosions

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

> ****POINT 6 — Raid Mechanics****

The only AoE pet ability is:

 **Gorilla Thunderstomp**

> ~200–320 damage
>  40 second cooldown

It is not viable.

So pets should focus on **single-target damage**.

That role is perfectly filled by the **Scorpion**.

Except:

> Some bosses reset poison stacks
>  Others are completely immune

In Karazhan 40 the scorpion becomes unusable in:

 **6 out of 9 bosses.**

The alternative is the **Wind Serpent**.

But it will be indirectly nerfed because the following combo disappears:

> Kill Command
>  Lightning Breath
>  Baited Shot

Without this burst the pet becomes extremely weak.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

> ****POINT 7 — Consumables and Buffs****

Pets can only use:

> Scrolls
>  Jujus

None of them increase:

 **Pet Spell Power**

Which is exactly what Scorpions and Wind Serpents need.

Meanwhile many buffs increase:

> Strength

content_html:
If you don’t know me, read this introduction. If you already know me, skip to point 1.
At the very end I will propose some realistic solutions related to the problems explained below.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Hello, I’m Skurridizo.

I’m one of the players who has explored hunter pets in Turtle WoW the most — if not the one who has done it the most.

I’m a huge fan of the class and currently have FOUR level 60 hunters across different Turtle WoW servers.

I also run two YouTube channels dedicated to sharing hunter knowledge specifically for Turtle WoW.

Right now I’m playing Survival more than any other spec in Karazhan 40 and Naxxramas, but until recently I always played:

Beast Mastery

This specialization rewards player skill through small details and makes it the most complex of the three specs — and in my opinion the most fun.

Unfortunately this talent tree is overshadowed by Survival, and many Karazhan 40 mechanics punish it heavily, almost as if the dungeon was designed specifically to discourage playing this spec.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
POINT 1 — Stable Slots
Many people think having 4 + 1 stable slots is more than enough.

The answer is obviously NO.

Just like tanks swap gear pieces for different situations, there is no single pet that is the best in every scenario.
Pet swapping is mandatory if you want to get real value from Beast Mastery.
Here are some examples of pets I tamed, leveled to 60, and eventually abandoned.

All of them are BiS within their family because they have the fastest attack speed.
• Broken Tooth (2 times) – Level 37 rare with ~7h respawn
• Spirit Fox (1 time) – Level 53 rare with +48h respawn
• Ravage (1 time) – Level 51 rare with 15h respawn
• Ravasaur Matriarch (2 times) – Level 53 rare with 15h respawn
• Gretheer (2 times) – Level 57 rare with 50h respawn
• Lavender Mana Wyrm – Level 7 Wind Serpent from the High Elf starting zone
BiS in PvP because its tiny size makes it almost invisible
This is only a small portion of the countless pets I had to find in their BiS version, spend hours leveling to 60, and later discover they were not actually worth it.

Ideally required pets:
• Bear — Support playstyle
• Wolf — AoE farming + offensive support
• Slow Raptor — BiS DPS for Marksmanship
• Fast Raptor — BiS DPS for Survival
• Fast Scorpion — BiS Beast Mastery DPS in most situations
• Slow Scorpion — BiS BM/MM DPS in many situations
• Wind Serpent — Best option when Scorpion doesn't work / BiS PvP BM
• Spider — BiS PvP outside Beast Mastery
• Cat — Required for some raid skips
• Cobra / Bat / Tallstrider — Solo content and niche situations
Everything else becomes forgotten or sub-optimal.

My current stable:
Bear
Fast Raptor
Wolf
Fast Scorpion
Slow Raptor
I am still missing several important ones.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
POINT 2 — Training Difficulty
In later expansions hunters could tame a low level pet and it would automatically scale to:

Player Level -5

Meaning you only needed to level the last five levels.

Now try leveling the BiS bear:

Ursol'Lok
Level 32 rare
15 hour respawn timer
What happens?
• You spend an entire day camping the spawn
• Then at least 10 hours leveling it to 60
• And it consumes a massive amount of food (gold)
I did this a few months ago.

Almost nobody else will do it because the effort does not justify the result compared to a regular Winterspring level 60 bear.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
POINT 3 — Talents That Don’t Fit
There are some items that increase pet damage such as:

https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60784
https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=22061

These were useful when you were a fresh level 60 raiding:
Molten Core
Onyxia
Blackwing Lair
But today the situation is simple:
+9 Agility already gives more value than increasing your pet damage.
Why does this happen?

In WoW Classic pets had almost no real scaling.

Turtle WoW introduced new talents that try to solve this.

The most important one is:

SPIRIT BOND
• 25% of your Ranged Attack Power → Pet Attack Power
• 15% of your Ranged Attack Power → Pet Spell Power
• Small health regeneration in combat
Beast Mastery revolves entirely around maximizing this talent.

Because of this, the pets that deal the most damage today are the ones that scale with Spell Power:
Cobra
Scorpion
Wind Serpent
Gorilla
The Gorilla can mostly be ignored because:
• Poor scaling
• 40 second cooldown ability
Current pet damage talents:
Improved Eyes of the Beast → +30% damage (but you stop attacking)
Unleashed Fury → +20% damage
Coordinated Assault → scales from hunter melee AP instead of pet
Ferocity → +15% crit
Frenzy → +30% attack speed
Spirit Bond
Baited Shot → +15% damage
Kill Command → GCD + huge mana cost
Only Spirit Bond actually scales with gear.

And that scaling is simply not enough for late-game content.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
POINT 4 — Late Game Gear Problems
Beast Mastery benefits most from Ranged Attack Power.

However many items in:
Naxxramas
Karazhan 40
trade attack power for critical strike.

This improves the hunter’s personal DPS but does almost nothing for the pet.

Additionally:
Tier 0.5
Tier 1
Tier 2
had useful defensive bonuses for pets.

These bonuses disappear completely in:
Tier 3
Tier 3.5
There is only one bonus:
+50 Attack Power for hunter and pet
But the current meta favors Spell Power scaling pets.

A survivability bonus for pets would be far more valuable.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
POINT 5 — Pet Survivability
In raids almost no healers keep pet frames visible.

So hunters are expected to heal their own pets.

The problem is the spell:

Mend Pet
5 second channel
480 mana
1225 total healing
20 yard range
This spell is extremely inefficient.

Even with the improved talent version it remains terrible.

A healer can outperform it with one instant GCD.

Because of this the most valuable skill becomes:

perfect pet positioning.

But many mechanics still kill pets regardless:
Void zones
Thaddius Tesla charges
Kruul cleave
Chess knight cleaves
Heigan explosions
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
POINT 6 — Raid Mechanics
The only AoE pet ability is:

Gorilla Thunderstomp
~200–320 damage
40 second cooldown
It is not viable.

So pets should focus on single-target damage.

That role is perfectly filled by the Scorpion.

Except:
Some bosses reset poison stacks
Others are completely immune
In Karazhan 40 the scorpion becomes unusable in:

6 out of 9 bosses.

The alternative is the Wind Serpent.

But it will be indirectly nerfed because the following combo disappears:
Kill Command
Lightning Breath
Baited Shot
Without this burst the pet becomes extremely weak.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
POINT 7 — Consumables and Buffs
Pets can only use:
Scrolls
Jujus
None of them increase:

Pet Spell Power

Which is exactly what Scorpions and Wind Serpents need.

Meanwhile many buffs increase:
Strength
Attack Power
Which again benefits the wrong pets.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
REALISTIC SOLUTIONS
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Solution 1 — Chimera Pet Family

Quest:

"Gotta Tame'em All!"

Requirement:

Learn every pet ability rank from every family.

Reward:

Ability to tame Chimeras.
Attack modifier: +15%
Health modifier: +5%
Armor modifier: +5%
(Current best base pet: Cobra → +13.5 / +3 / +3)

Chimeras could learn abilities from every pet family.

This would solve:
Stable slot problems
Training problems
Testing difficulty
Combat versatility
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Solution 2 — Improve Pet Healing Talents

Current talents lack synergy:
Improved Mend Pet
Improved Revive Pet
Improved Eyes of the Beast
Proposed redesign:
Improved Mend Pet
→ 20→25 / 40→50% healing
→ dispel chance each tick

NEW:
Pet deals 15→30% more damage while channeling
and regenerates 15→30% more focus
Improved Revive Pet

Cast time reduced by 3→6 sec
Mana cost reduced by 20→40%

NEW:
Mend Pet range increased by 15→30 yards
Improved Eyes of the Beast

Duration increased by 30→60 sec

NEW:
Pet melee and ability range +2→3 yards
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Solution 3 — Improve Scaling
Increase Spirit Bond:
15→30% Ranged AP → Pet Attack Power
10→20% Ranged AP → Pet Spell Power
New talents:

Bloody Attacks
2% of pet damage returned as healing
Cunning Skills
• Pet gains 25% of hunter crit chance
• Pet gains AP and Spell Power equal to 25% of hunter Intelligence
• Pet copies hunter consumable buffs
This roughly translates to:
+5–10% pet crit
+60 AP / Spell Power
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════
FINAL CONCLUSION
These are relatively small changes that would dramatically improve the quality of life for Beast Mastery.

Ironically the next patch introduces:

Aspect of the Viper

because some hunters struggle with mana.

But Tallstriders already solved that problem.

The real solution was never new crazy abilities.

The real solution is letting hunters craft their own strategies through pets that scale properly.
Pet base stats and abilities could also be reviewed to make more families viable.

content_md:
I agree that the chimera solution proposed is not the way to go. Pet families need a rebalance and while Skurridizo is right (it won't be easy), it must be the way going forward. Many interesting abilities like Pack Ally were introduced but it didn't change the fact that hyenas, for instance, have no niche.

That said, yes, we should tame chimeras and many more beasts ([viewtopic.php?p=150953#p150953](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=150953#p150953))!

The main issue with pets is their survival. As the OP lays out, they're often ignored by healers for both healing and dispelling. Solutions to the problem are:

 - Avoidance affects cleaves and chain lightnings and is buffed to 90%. Any DoT applied through AoE is always reduced, as well

 - Mend Pet becomes a HoT like its TBC version

 - A talent deep in the BM tree giving vampirism to the pet through either the pet's own damage, the hunter's or both

 - Pets should melee the target from max melee distance when sent to attack when they are outside melee range. More often than not, a pet will go dead center of a target's hitbox and this can cause trouble with cleaves or attacks like shadowflame. This behavior is observed in bosses such as Nefarian, the BWL drakes, Ragnaros, Omen or Solnius but funnily not on Onyxia: pets do attack from max distance there. Any hunter doing Nefarian will quickly realize how disruptive this problem is, especially when combined with the continuous fears that displace the pet.

On the other hand, the BM tree is bloated with 5-point talent nodes: after starting the 3rd row, there's not a single point to spare on *any* utility talent, not even Intimidation! This is relevant because if Mend Pet became a HoT, for instance, then the talent that provides a dispel would become quite attractive but PvE BM hunters would not be able to take it.

Talents such as Ferocity should have a total of 3/3 while keeping the overall same amount of damage increase. Frenzy should just be 1 or at most 2 points. In the history of Vanilla, TBC, WotLK, SoD and any fanmade variations, Frenzy has **never** been completely filled and at most had a total of 3 out of 5 points.

The incoming new talent tree worsens this situation by having a second-to-last row with a total of 9 talent points... on a class that *needs* 20 points for another tree if going ranged! No other class or spec in the game has these restrictions. For instance, rogues require less points to reach the desired crit damage talent in the Assassination tree, whereas warriors only need 2 points to fill Impale in the Arms tree.

I have provided more feedback on the upcoming changes here [viewtopic.php?p=166396#p166396](https://forum.turtlecraft.gg/viewtopic.php?p=166396#p166396), as well as the original post I quote there but I won't go into detail in this thread because it's not the focus.

However, I will say that the incoming Kill Command could be another tuning knob when it comes to pet families. What if KC had damage and effects that varied based on family? For instance, what if a hyena using KC would reduce the CD of Pack Ally by a certain amount of seconds? If KC is released as is, it's going to be one of the most, if not *the* most, underwhelming capstones of all specs in the game (it's weaker than Coordinated Assault, an 11-point talent!). But if it had a change like this one, then it'd be quite thematic and useful, and it would help balance pet families in other ways.

I also agree with Skurridizo when it comes to pet scaling. Having Spirit Bond (or any other talent) transform our intellect stat into pet damage is an interesting way of influencing gearing a bit besides only desiring raw agility. In my opinion, 30% of the hunter's total crit should benefit the pet as well as 100% of the haste from gear (so no quiver, quick shots/strikes or rapid fire). This would make scaling for BM more in line with other non-caster DPS specs.

Regardless, it's clear that something has to be done. We need more stable slots, more tameables, a better pet leveling system, and a proper look at pet survival. Hopefully, the developers will act sooner than later. TWoW is the only Classic type server that is going in the right direction when it comes to pets but there's still a long way to go.

This would make scaling for BM more in line with other non-caster DPS specs.

Regardless, it's clear that something has to be done. We need more stable slots, more tameables, a better pet leveling system, and a proper look at pet survival. Hopefully, the developers will act sooner than later. TWoW is the only Classic type server that is going in the right direction when it comes to pets but there's still a long way to go.

I could just tune the positioning by doing the attack > return > attack in this case and it's fine but the position command should not be bugged either way.

And the problem I outlined above for Omen would persist anyway. I haven't found any other boss as annoying as this one yet though.

> Avoidance does **not** work properly. Cleaves, such as those from bosses like Vaelastrasz, Omen, Onyxia... they all deal FULL damage to the pet. Cleaves and chain lightnings are AoEs and so should be affected by avoidance.

Avoidance is working properly, the problem is that damage is calculated individually. They add like an individual dot when you stay in an area, that is why the pets take full damage. I know its not easy to understand, but those are not considered AoE damage, just a single target calculated damage applied to all the people in an area.

You can try for example in a duel against a Survival hunter to repeat these steps and you will see:

Hunter SV places an Explosive Trap -> AoE Fire damage
You step over the trap next to your pet

You will see your pet taking less damage from the initial tic of damage, but the dots are the same for you and your pet

And this is not an avoidance's issue, its how about those attacks are coded. Avoidance works completely fine and what you see are just individual calculations of damage.

Si no me conoces, lee esta introducción. Si me conoces pasa al punto 1. Al final del todo propongo soluciones que vienen relacionadas con lo que explicaré abajo sobre los problemas actuales. Hola, soy Skurridizo. Soy uno de los jugadores que más ha profundizado en explorar el tema de las pets en Turtle wow si es que no soy el que más. Soy un fanático de la clase y actualmente tengo CUATRO cazadores a nivel 60 entre varios servidores de Turtle WoW. También tengo dos canales de YouTube dedicados a compartir conocimiento del cazador dedicado a Turtle WoW. Ahora mismo estoy jugando más Survival que cualquier otra rama en el contenido de Karazhan 40 y Naxxramas, pero hasta no hace mucho siempre he jugado Beast Mastery, ya que esta rama es la que más recompensa la habilidad del jugador en pequeños detalles y la convierte en la más compleja de las 3 y a mi gusto la más divertida. Tristemente, es una rama de talentos que se ve opacada por la rama de Survival y bastantes mecánicas de Karazhan 40 te penalizan demasiado, casi pareciendo que la dungeon se hizo expresamente para no jugar esta rama de talentos. Punto 1: Los huecos en el establo Mucha gente pensará que tener 4 + 1 huecos en el establo son más que suficientes y la respuesta es obviamente NO ¿Por qué? Al igual que los tanques se cambian partes de su equipo para diferentes situaciones, no existe ninguna pet que sea la mejor en todas las situaciones. El hecho de tener versatilidad a la hora de poder cambiarte de pet es algo obligatorio si se le quiere sacar rendimiento a esta especialización. Os pondré un ejemplo de pets que he tenido a nivel 60 y las he acabado abandonando. Todas estas son BiS dentro de su familia, ya que son las que más velocidad de ataque tienen entre sus semejantes. Broken Tooth, 2 veces. Rare de nivel 37 con 7h de respawn. Spirit Fox, 1 vez. Rare de nivel 53 con +48h de respawn. Ravage, 1 vez. Rare de nivel 51 con 15h de respawn. Ravasaur Matriarch, 2 veces. Rare de nivel 53 con 15h de respawn. Gretheer, 2 veces. Rare de nivel 57 con 50h de respawn. Lavender Mana Wyrm, 1 vez. Una Wind Serpent normal de la zona de inicio de los High Elf de nivel 7. Es BiS por su tamaño enano que la hace prácticamente imperceptible en PVP Esto es una pequeña parte de las incontables pets que he tenido que buscar en su versión BiS, pasarme unas tantas horas leveando hasta nivel 60 para luego comprobar que no son buenas. ¿Qué pets serían idealmente necesarias? - Oso: Para jugar en una versión de apoyo - Lobo: Para el farmeo en AoE y una versión de apoyo un poco más ofensiva - Raptor de velocidad de ataque lenta: BiS para hacer DPS si vas de Marksmanship - Raptor de velocidad de ataque rápida: BiS para hacer DPS si vas de Survival - Escorpión rápido: BiS para hacer DPS de Beast Mastery en la mayoría de ocasiones - Escorpión lento: BiS para hacer DPS de BM-MM en la mayoría de ocasiones - Serpiente de Viento: Suele ser la mejor opción cuando no funciona el escorpión y BiS PVP en talentos BM - Araña: BiS para PVP cuando no vas de Beast Mastery - Felino: Necesario para hacer algunos skips en raid - Cobra, Murciélago y Avestruz: Sirven para hacer contenido en solitario y en ciertas situaciones específicas Todas las demás, quedan en el olvido o son sub óptimas. En mi establo actualme tengo: Oso, Raptor rápido, Lobo, Escorpión rápido y Raptor lento. Echo en falta unas cuantas. Punto 2: La dificultad del entrenamiento En versiones posteriores, se añadió que cuando un hunter podía tamear una pet de nivel bajo, esta automáticamente se subía a cinco niveles debajo del jugador, por lo que sólo hacía falta levearla los 5 últimos niveles. Os propongo simplemente que intentéis levear el oso BiS Ursol'Lok, unrare de 15 horas de respawn de nivel 32. Tendrás que estar un día entero campeando el spot y luego te llevará mínimo 10 horas de gameplay subirlo a nivel 60. Por el camino se va a comer un camión de comida, lo cual cuesta oro ¿Aceptáis el reto? Yo lo hice hace unos cuantos meses y os aseguro que no veréis muchos más que lo hayan hecho porque obviamente el esfuerzo no recompensa la diferencia de resultados con un oso normal de nivel 60 de Winterspring. Punto 3: Talentos que no encajan Existen algunos objetos que aumentan el daño que realiza tu pet como <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60784> <https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=22061> Eran útiles cuando eras fresh nivel 60, raideando en Molten Core, Onyxia y Black Wing Lair funcionaban y estaban bien, pero el problema es que un item que aporte +9 de agilidad, ya es mejor que ese bonus de aumentarle el daño a la pet. ¿Por qué sucede esto? En WoW classic no existía un escalado real de las pets, esta era la única manera de aumentar su daño. En Turtle WoW tenemos unas grandes adiciones a la rama de talentos que permiten que sea viable en fases más tardías del contenido. La joya de la corona es el talento SPIRIT BOND Quien no sepa lo que hace, Un 25% de nuestro Ranged Attack Power se lo da a la pet en forma de Attack Power y un 15% de nuestro Ranged Attack Power se lo da a la pet en forma de Spell Power. Además otorga una pequeña regeneración de vida, aun estando en comabate.La rama de Beast Mastery gira en torno a este talento y en sacarle el máximo provecho posible. Este es el motivo, por el que a día de hoy las pets que hacen más daño con esta combinación de talentos son las que escalan por Spell Power, que son 4. Cobra, Escorpión, Wind Serpent y Gorilla. El Gorilla podríamos ignorarlo porque su habilidad tiene un escalado casi nulo y 40 segundos de Cool Down para hacer menos daño que otras de 10 segundos de Cool Down. En los talentos actuales, tenemos la siguiente lista para aumentar el daño de la pet: Improved Eyes of the Beast: +30% *** Dejas de atacar si lo canalizas xddd Unleashed Fury: +20% Coordinated Assault: Hace daño por el MELEE ATTACK POWER DEL HUNTER y no de la pet xddd Ferocity: +15% de crítico Frenzy: +30% Attack Speed Spirit Bond: Citado anteriormente Baited Shot: Aumenta el daño de la pet un 15% al objetivo Kill Command: Habilidad activable que interrumpe tu rotación con un GCD y un gasto de maná exagerademente alto para un aumento pobre de DPS Hay otros talentos que generan un poco de utilidad, pero salvo Bestial Precision que le da hit y weapon skill, los demás no rentan. Como veis, ninguno de estos aumenta un escalado progresivo con el equipo del cazador salvo Spirit Bond, que no es suficiente para el contenido en late game. Los nuevos talentos de Beast Mastery que se han filtrado, me parecen un nerfeo a la especialización que es a día de hoy menos jugada y que para que rinda de manera aceptable hace falta un dominio muy grande. Link a los talentos nuevos <https://www.talent-builder.dev/tree/qPngf49SEV> Volvemos a tener un talento que hace lo mismo que Coordinated Assault y sospecho que estará bugeado y escalará mejor en un Survival que en un Beast Mastery. Más talentos copy paste de aumentar en % el daño base de la pet, pero que realmente +1% de daño a la pet ya es inferior a +3 de agilidad al jugador y más aún cuando se activan de manera azarosa. Se pierde el antiguo Kill Command, el cuál tenía dos utilidades: La primera era hacer una gran sinergia con Baited Shot, de donde salía un tremendo combo con la Wind Serpent La segunda es ser una habilidad defensiva de bajo cool down para quitarle el CC a la pet Ahora el anti CC tendrá un enorme Cool Down, pero la mejora de daño me parece que va a ser muy potente con jugadores de nivel fresh 60, pero no va a escalar a penas nada conforme avance el contenido del juego. De hecho este talento en combinación al nuevo Kill Command, me parecen mucho peores que la combinación actual de Kill Command + Baited Shot. En torno al 60% del daño le pertenece al cazador yendo en bestias a día de hoy, por lo que el daño de Baited Shot es una gran aportación que ni por asomo se le van a acercar los nuevos Kill Command + Bestial Wrath. El cazador no necesita más talentos que aumenten porcentualmente el daño de la pet, necesita un mejor escalado de Spirit Bond u otros talentos que escalen con otro stat, ya sea inteligencia, crítico, haste, espíritu o cualquier cosa que se os ocurra. Punto 4: Equipo de late game y discordancia con los talentos Como ya hemos visto, los talentos de bestias se exprimen más cuando el equipo te proporciona mucho Ranged Attack Power, pero como vamos viendo, hay muchas piezas en Naxxramas y Karazhan 40, que nos proporcionan crítico a cambio de sacrificar un poquito de attack power. Obviamente, en cuanto a daño individual del cazador compensa totalmente este intercambio, pero para la pet es una estadística que escala por otra que no escala. Además de eso los tier 0,5, 1 y 2 aportan bonus bastante interesantes a la pet en temas defensivos. Se echan en falta estos bonus en los sets 3 y 3.5. Es cierto que hay un bonus de 4 piezas del tier 3 que proporciona +50 Attack Power al cazador y la pet, pero recordemos que el meta favorece a las pets de Spell Power para cuando eres Beast Mastery y se echa en falta un bonus de supervivencia a la pet. Punto 5: Supervivencia de la pet En cuanto a las raids, pocos healers (o ninguno en pugs) juegan con el frame de pets a la vista para poder curarlas. Y bien, la mayoría pensaréis que es obligación del hunter curar a su pet. Este es el hechizo para curar a la pet Mend Pet: 5 segundos de canalización y 480 de maná para una curación total de 1225. Tiene 20 yardas de rango, por lo que ya la distancia lo limita además de lo ineficiente que es. Es terriblemente malo, no hay manera de hacerlo funcionar de manera correcta. Es cierto que hay un talento que aumenta la curación un 40% y le da la probabilidad de dispelear. Este talento sería útil si otorgara más rango al hechizo y le proporcionara a la pet un daño extra mientras estamos CANALIZANDO CINCO SEGUNDOS DE DPS para hacer una cura que un healer te la hace con un GCD instantáneo y 150 de maná. Ya que es inviable dedicarse a curar tu pet, lo más valioso es protegerla y moverla bien. Lo cual es algo de lo que yo personalmente me siento orgulloso porque he masterizado, pero he de admitir que es una tarea muy compleja y en ocasiones estresante, que además se ve penalizada por mecánicas de daño a multi objetivo calculado de manera individual y no se reduce por su Avoidance. Ejemplos de estos daños son: Void zones, Thaddius tesla charges, Kruuls cleave, Chess' knights cleaves, Heigan's explosions... Punto 6: Mecánicas de raid Actualmente la única habilidad de AoE que hay en las pets es el Thunderstomp del Gorilla, el cuál hará entre 200 y 320 de daño (dependiendo de si eres BM o no) y tendrá 40 segundos de Cool Down. Es inviable usar una habilidad así teniendo en cuenta que el Gorilla no ofrece absolutamente nada más que eso. No tiene modificador de daño positivo ni ningún ataque potente. Por lo que si las pets no tienen daño en AoE para el trash, lo lógico sería enfocarlo a single target para bosses. Casualmente está el escorpión que cumple este rol a la perfección y lo hace estupendamente bien, de no ser porque hay bosses que tienen diferentes fases de golpeo y resetean sus marcas de veneno o porque hay varios de ellos en Karazhan40 que literalmente son inmunes al veneno. El escorpión se hace inviable en 6 de los 9 bosses de Karazhan y la Wind Serpent que sería la opción ideal para esas 6 peleas donde el escorpión no rinde va a ser nerfeado en el próximo parche ¿Por qué un nerf si no le cambian nada a la Wind Serpent? Porque se va a eliminar su combo de Kill Command + Lightning Breath + Baited Shot, lo cual es un burst enorme y lo que hace viable a esta pet, sin este combo se queda muy baja en daño y habrá que confiar en los golpes blancos de una cobra xd o en un raptor que no termina de brillar con talentos de Beast Mastery. Punto 7: Consumibles y Buffs Los únicos consumibles que pueden usarse sobre una pet son los Scrolls y Jujus. No es gran cosa, pero es algo. Ninguno de estos consumibles aumentan el Spell Power de la pet que es lo que necesitan tanto el Escorpión como la Wind Serpent. De igual manera pasa con los buffs, no hay ninguno que aumente el Spell Power de la pet, pero en cambio tenemos muchos de ellos que o bien aumentan su fuerza o bien aumentan su attack power. SOLUCIONES REALISTAS A LOS PROBLEMAS: Solución 1 Lo ideal sería que las pets pudieran aprender ataques de otras familias, pero para hacer una única pet que solucione varias cosas a la vez es la siguiente: Mision: Gotta Tame'em All! Se requiere al jugador aprender todos los ataques de las pets de todos los rangos. Una vez completado, te permitiría tamear Chimeras. Nueva familia de pet: Chimera Bonificador de Ataque: +15% Bonificador de Salud: +5% Bonificador de Armadura: +5% Recordemos que actualmente la pet con atributos base más altos es la cobra con +13.5%, +3% y +3%. Sería una versión ligeramente superior. Las Chimeras podrían aprender todos los ataques de todos los rangos, lo cuál solucionaría los problemas de huecos en el establo, entrenamiento, facilidad de testeo y versatilidad en combate. Se le va a añadir un aspecto al cazador para el tema del maná, cuando ya hay una pet que hace eso. Podría optarse por una pet con un montón de habilidades de apoyo o incluso habilidades defensivas para esos momentos críticos de raid Solución 2 Mejorar los talentos para sanar a la pet Actualmente hay 3 talentos que van enfocados a generar utilidad en la pet, pero no tienen sinergia con nada, que son: Improved Mend pet: Aumenta la curación de Mend Pet en un 40% y da un 20% por cada tic de hacer un dispell. Ya hemos mencionado arriba las carencias de esta habilidad. Improved Revive pet: Reduce el tiempo de casteo de 10 segundos a 4 segundos y reduce el coste de maná de la habilidad Improved Eyes of the beast: Aumenta su duración de 1 a 2 minutos y aumenta el daño que hace la pet mientras se canaliza en un +30% Eyes of the Beast es un hechizo que sirve para la utilidad de poder controlar la pet, pero para daño implica estar renunciando al 60% de tu DPS para aumentar un 25% (tenemos Unleashed Fury) el DPS de tu pet que representa el 40%. En combate no tiene mucha utilidad salvo alguna triquiñuela específica que quieras buscar. Los talentos quedarían así Improved Mend pet: Aumenta la curación de Mend Pet en un 40% y da un 20% por cada tic de hacer un dispell. Ya hemos mencionado arriba las carencias de esta habilidad. Improved Revive pet: Reduce el tiempo de casteo de 10 segundos a 4 segundos y reduce el coste de maná de la habilidad Improved Eyes of the beast: Aumenta su duración de 1 a 2 minutos y aumenta el daño que hace la pet mientras se canaliza en un +30% Los talentos pasarían a tener el siguiente efecto Improved Mend pet: Increases the amount you heal your pet with Mend Pet by 20->25/40->50% and gives the spell a 15/50% of cleansing 1 Curse, Disease, Magic or Poison effect from the pet each tick. NEW While channeling Eyes of the Beast or Mend pet, your pet deals 15/30% additional damage and gains 15/30% increased focus regeneration. Improved Revive pet: Revive Pet's casting time is reduced by 3/6 sec, mana cost is reduced by 20/40%. and increases the health your pet returns by an additional 15/30% NEW Increases the range of your spell Mend Pet by 15/30 yards. Improved Eyes of the Beast: Increases the duration of Eyes of the beast by 30/60 sec. NEW Increases your pet's melee attacks and abilities range by 2/3 yards. Solución 3 Añadir algo más de escalados y eliminar los nuevos talentos que aumentarán el daño de la pet en porcentaje base. Aumentar el efecto de Spirit Bond Your pet gains melee attack power equal to 12->15/25->30% of your ranged attack power and spell power equal to 7.5->10/15->20% of your ranged attack power. While your pet is active, you and your pet will regenerate 1/2% of total health every 5 sec. Añadir dos nuevos talentos: Bloody Attacks: Your pet gains 2% of damage dealt is returned as healing Cunning Skills: Your pet gains Critical Hit Chance equal to 25% of your Ranged Critical Hit chance Your pet gains Attack Power and Spell Power equal to 25% of your Intelligence Puede parecer demasiado, pero es raro que un Hunter llegue a 40% de probabilidad de crítico en raid y con todos los consumibles. En cuanto a inteligencia, en raid y consumibles se podría alcanzar aproximadamente 250. En total tendríamos entre un +5 y +10% de crítico a la pet y un +60 de Attack Power y Spell power. CONCLUSIÓN FINAL Son pequeños cambios que mejorarían mucho la calidad de vida de esta especialización. Fijáos que en el nuevo parche se va a otorgar el Aspect of the Viper porque les falta maná a los cazadores que no saben jugar bien su clase y tienen poco equipo, cuando ya teníamos la pasiva del Tallstrider para hacer eso. La solución no estaba en inventarse nuevas pasivas de ataques locos, sino el permitir cocinar a cada uno su propia estrategia con diferentes ataques de la pet y hacer que pueda escalar correctamente. También se podría hacer una revisión de los stats base de las pets y de muchas de las habilidades para hacerlas funcionar. Si no me conoces, lee esta introducción. Si me conoces pasa al punto 1. Al final del todo propongo soluciones que vienen relacionadas con lo que explicaré abajo sobre los problemas actuales. Hola, soy Skurridizo. Soy uno de los jugadores que más ha profundizado en explorar el tema de las pets en Turtle wow si es que no soy el que más. Soy un fanático de la clase y actualmente tengo CUATRO cazadores a nivel 60 entre varios servidores de Turtle WoW. También tengo dos canales de YouTube dedicados a compartir conocimiento del cazador dedicado a Turtle WoW. Ahora mismo estoy jugando más Survival que cualquier otra rama en el contenido de Karazhan 40 y Naxxramas, pero hasta no hace mucho siempre he jugado Beast Mastery, ya que esta rama es la que más recompensa la habilidad del jugador en pequeños detalles y la convierte en la más compleja de las 3 y a mi gusto la más divertida. Tristemente, es una rama de talentos que se ve opacada por la rama de Survival y bastantes mecánicas de Karazhan 40 te penalizan demasiado, casi pareciendo que la dungeon se hizo expresamente para no jugar esta rama de talentos. Punto 1: Los huecos en el establo Mucha gente pensará que tener 4 + 1 huecos en el establo son más que suficientes y la respuesta es obviamente NO ¿Por qué? Al igual que los tanques se cambian partes de su equipo para diferentes situaciones, no existe ninguna pet que sea la mejor en todas las situaciones. El hecho de tener versatilidad a la hora de poder cambiarte de pet es algo obligatorio si se le quiere sacar rendimiento a esta especialización. Os pondré un ejemplo de pets que he tenido a nivel 60 y las he acabado abandonando. Todas estas son BiS dentro de su familia, ya que son las que más velocidad de ataque tienen entre sus semejantes. Broken Tooth, 2 veces. Rare de nivel 37 con 7h de respawn. Spirit Fox, 1 vez. Rare de nivel 53 con +48h de respawn. Ravage, 1 vez. Rare de nivel 51 con 15h de respawn. Ravasaur Matriarch, 2 veces. Rare de nivel 53 con 15h de respawn. Gretheer, 2 veces. Rare de nivel 57 con 50h de respawn. Lavender Mana Wyrm, 1 vez. Una Wind Serpent normal de la zona de inicio de los High Elf de nivel 7. Es BiS por su tamaño enano que la hace prácticamente imperceptible en PVP Esto es una pequeña parte de las incontables pets que he tenido que buscar en su versión BiS, pasarme unas tantas horas leveando hasta nivel 60 para luego comprobar que no son buenas. ¿Qué pets serían idealmente necesarias? - Oso: Para jugar en una versión de apoyo - Lobo: Para el farmeo en AoE y una versión de apoyo un poco más ofensiva - Raptor de velocidad de ataque lenta: BiS para hacer DPS si vas de Marksmanship - Raptor de velocidad de ataque rápida: BiS para hacer DPS si vas de Survival - Escorpión rápido: BiS para hacer DPS de Beast Mastery en la mayoría de ocasiones - Escorpión lento: BiS para hacer DPS de BM-MM en la mayoría de ocasiones - Serpiente de Viento: Suele ser la mejor opción cuando no funciona el escorpión y BiS PVP en talentos BM - Araña: BiS para PVP cuando no vas de Beast Mastery - Felino: Necesario para hacer algunos skips en raid - Cobra, Murciélago y Avestruz: Sirven para hacer contenido en solitario y en ciertas situaciones específicas Todas las demás, quedan en el olvido o son sub óptimas. En mi establo actualme tengo: Oso, Raptor rápido, Lobo, Escorpión rápido y Raptor lento. Echo en falta unas cuantas. Punto 2: La dificultad del entrenamiento En versiones posteriores, se añadió que cuando un hunter podía tamear una pet de nivel bajo, esta automáticamente se subía a cinco niveles debajo del jugador, por lo que sólo hacía falta levearla los 5 últimos niveles. Os propongo simplemente que intentéis levear el oso BiS Ursol'Lok, unrare de 15 horas de respawn de nivel 32. Tendrás que estar un día entero campeando el spot y luego te llevará mínimo 10 horas de gameplay subirlo a nivel 60. Por el camino se va a comer un camión de comida, lo cual cuesta oro ¿Aceptáis el reto? Yo lo hice hace unos cuantos meses y os aseguro que no veréis muchos más que lo hayan hecho porque obviamente el esfuerzo no recompensa la diferencia de resultados con un oso normal de nivel 60 de Winterspring. Punto 3: Talentos que no encajan Existen algunos objetos que aumentan el daño que realiza tu pet como https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=60784 https://database.turtlecraft.gg/?item=22061 Eran útiles cuando eras fresh nivel 60, raideando en Molten Core, Onyxia y Black Wing Lair funcionaban y estaban bien, pero el problema es que un item que aporte +9 de agilidad, ya es mejor que ese bonus de aumentarle el daño a la pet. ¿Por qué sucede esto? En WoW classic no existía un escalado real de las pets, esta era la única manera de aumentar su daño. En Turtle WoW tenemos unas grandes adiciones a la rama de talentos que permiten que sea viable en fases más tardías del contenido. La joya de la corona es el talento SPIRIT BOND Quien no sepa lo que hace, Un 25% de nuestro Ranged Attack Power se lo da a la pet en forma de Attack Power y un 15% de nuestro Ranged Attack Power se lo da a la pet en forma de Spell Power. Además otorga una pequeña regeneración de vida, aun estando en comabate.La rama de Beast Mastery gira en torno a este talento y en sacarle el máximo provecho posible. Este es el motivo, por el que a día de hoy las pets que hacen más daño con esta combinación de talentos son las que escalan por Spell Power, que son 4. Cobra, Escorpión, Wind Serpent y Gorilla. El Gorilla podríamos ignorarlo porque su habilidad tiene un escalado casi nulo y 40 segundos de Cool Down para hacer menos daño que otras de 10 segundos de Cool Down. Como veis, ninguno de estos aumenta un escalado progresivo con el equipo del cazador salvo Spirit Bond, que no es suficiente para el contenido en late game. Los nuevos talentos de Beast Mastery que se han filtrado, me parecen un nerfeo a la especialización que es a día de hoy menos jugada y que para que rinda de manera aceptable hace falta un dominio muy grande. While your pet is active, you and your pet will regenerate 1/2% of total health every 5 sec. Añadir dos nuevos talentos: Bloody Attacks: Your pet gains 2% of damage dealt is returned as healing Cunning Skills: Your pet gains Critical Hit Chance equal to 25% of your Ranged Critical Hit chance Your pet gains Attack Power and Spell Power equal to 25% of your Intelligence Puede parecer demasiado, pero es raro que un Hunter llegue a 40% de probabilidad de crítico en raid y con todos los consumibles. En cuanto a inteligencia, en raid y consumibles se podría alcanzar aproximadamente 250. En total tendríamos entre un +5 y +10% de crítico a la pet y un +60 de Attack Power y Spell power. CONCLUSIÓN FINAL Son pequeños cambios que mejorarían mucho la calidad de vida de esta especialización. Fijáos que en el nuevo parche se va a otorgar el Aspect of the Viper porque les falta maná a los cazadores que no saben jugar bien su clase y tienen poco equipo, cuando ya teníamos la pasiva del Tallstrider para hacer eso. La solución no estaba en inventarse nuevas pasivas de ataques locos, sino el permitir cocinar a cada uno su propia estrategia con diferentes ataques de la pet y hacer que pueda escalar correctamente. También se podría hacer una revisión de los stats base de las pets y de muchas de las habilidades para hacerlas funcionar. Si has llegado hasta aquí responde con este emoji en los comentarios y sabremos que lo has visto.
